newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 3.

text.p: THE DOMINION

The National Party's campaign to portray the New Zealand economy at risk if it was voted out took a serious hit when rating agency Standard and Poor's said it did not regard the election as a threat to New Zealand's AA+ credit rating.

Standard and Poor's sovereign risk managing director David Beer told a New York audience there could be a slowdown in economic reform after the election but a new government was not likely to depart drastically from current policies. Page 1.
Voting in the election could be postponed if the court challenge by the Republican Party succeeds. They are seeking the right to compete fully in the first MMP poll. Page 1.

National is fighting to recover its poise after what insiders say has been a disastrous 10 days on the election trail. Of most concern has been Prime Minister Jim Bolger's apparent loss of confidence last week, culminating in his dismal performance in the TVNZ leaders debate. Page 2.
Buoyant Labour leader Helen Clark campaigned in her party's stronghold of Dunedin, accusing Prime Minister Jim Bolger of running scared of her as he steps up his attacks on Labour. Page 2.

Television New Zealand would not back down on its plan to widen its final influential leaders debate to seven party leaders, despite a threat by New Zealand First leader Winston Peters not to take part. Page 2.

Brierley Investments would net a "modest surplus" from the selldown of its stake in British hotel group Thistle despite a loss on the sale of the shares, a company spokesman said. BIL will gross about NZ$174.5 million on the sale of 46 million shares at NZ$3.80 each. Page 17.
International rating agency Standard and Poor has reaffirmed its A long-term and A-1 commercial paper credit ratings on Tui milk products. Page 17.
State-owned Coal Corporation has bought its first low-grade lignite coal mine in Southland, for an undisclosed sum, from Carter Holt Harvey. Page 17.
Computer and Software supplier Wang New Zealand has bought Auckland's Imaging Solutions. Page 17.
Dutch postal and telecom group Royal PTT Nederland (KPN) would assess any possible breakup of TNT assets if its NZ$2.26 billion takeover bid succeeded, chairman Wim Dik said. Page 17.
A Singapore company has scrapped plans to buy and redevelop the Marsden B power station, saying power prices are too low to justify the project. Page 19.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

The government is on the verge of settling its largest deal with Maori, offering more than NZ$170 million for a large part of South Island tribe Ngai Tahu's domain. However, a major stumbling block is the crown's attempt to extinguish the tribe's customary fishing rights. Page 1.

National's election campaign has turned sharply aggressive with renewed attempts to scare voters over prospects under a centre-left government and a series of "hard sell" television adverts. Prime Minister Jim Bolger criticised financial markets for being too casual about the effects of a centre-left government.
Television New Zeland continued to defend itself from accusations that National had nobbled it to make changes to the final leaders' debate.

Brierley Investments' biggest asset, Thistle hotel group, has once again failed to come up to stratch, with the pricing for a much-hyped float falling flat. Few picked the price would end up at the bottom of the 170 pence (NZ$3.80) to 210 pence range.
All government stock yields from two to 10 years finished below 8 percent for the first time since February as rumours of more Samurai and Eurokiwi bond issues swept the money market.
The 160 cents a share takeover bid for Transmark Corporation will proceed despite the offer falling well short of an independent valuation of between 200 cents and 215 cents.

Dutch telecommunications and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV started a NZ$2.26 billion takeover bid for Australia's biggesst transport group TNT, aiming to create Europe's largest fast-post business.

Ratings agency Standard and Poor's has warned that New Zealand's economic reforms may stall for some months after the election, but it was not likely to threaten the country's AA+ foreign currency rating.
-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
